# Real application pages — 2026-10-28

Four real pages are the headline suite. The counter, 1,000-row fixture and krausest remain microbenchmarks; no losing micro case was removed.

Base: 9ccb50076580e6f32c83f3152b3bd367c71646d7. Browser: 156.0.8078.48. Node: v26.5.1. CPU: Apple M4 Pro.
Started: 2026-10-28T21:51:02.053Z. Repeats: 5 per lane/page/condition, rotating interleaved lane order.

Uptime before: 23:51  up 7 days, 15:56, 3 users, load averages: 2.47 8.72 9.70
Uptime after: 23:55  up 7 days, 16 hrs, 3 users, load averages: 3.11 5.25 7.82
Sample load1 range: 2.25–4.96. Host was not assumed quiet.

## Method

Uses resume-bench's existing production builders, pinned stable/preview resolution, build-manifest freshness checks, no-store Brotli loopback server and Chrome target. Each sample opens a fresh browser context; viewport 1280×800; caches disabled. One server at a time on port 4520 (configurable within 4520–4529). No new toolchains. Rivet, Solid 1/2 and Qwik 1/2 have identical generated product markup, CSS, data and algorithms; framework markers/state/scripts differ and count toward bytes. The handwritten rivet-derived research spike is retained as a micro fixture, not presented as a production framework. There is no React/Next lane in resume-bench.

Products: 48 visible cards from 96 server records, chips, search, price sort, two pages, header cart. Dashboard: four KPI cards, 50 visible rows from 100 server records, sort/pagination, tabs, menu and date controls. Settings: 15 fields, required/email validation, two toggles, cancel/confirm modal. Article: 12 sections, 48 paragraphs, TOC, search dialog, 12 copy buttons. No icon assets or external network dependencies. Server data is serialized by each framework, never imported into client bundles. All use whole-page native framework boundaries with no lane-specific behavioral shortcut. See real-pages/fixture.ts and contract.ts.

Initial SSR DOM signatures (tags, product attributes, normalized text) must agree across lanes and survive hydration. The behavioral gate exercises every control, empty filters, pagination reset, invalid/valid submission, cancellation, clipboard content and anchor navigation. Invalid lane/page cells are withheld, with errors below. Timed actions: products add-to-cart, dashboard descending sort, settings invalid submit, article open-search. These actions are trusted mouse clicks; input-to-paint uses the existing rAF then MessageChannel proxy after the expected DOM change. This includes the existing first-mouse-click deferral contract, unchanged. It is not a raw compositor presentation timestamp.

Fast is unthrottled. Slow is the existing Slow 4G profile (150 ms latency, 1.6 Mbps down, 750 kbps up) plus 4× CPU. Before-input window ends after load + 1,000 ms. HTML bytes are UTF-8 source bytes; HTML transfer and external JS bytes use CDP encodedDataLength (compressed transfer including headers). Inline executable script bytes are shown separately and are already included in HTML. JS requests include JavaScript preload/prefetch responses completed before input. CPU is CDP TaskDuration before input (renderer main-thread task time, not server CPU). FCP/LCP are browser observers up to the input cutoff; TBT is sum(max(long-task duration − 50 ms, 0)) from FCP to cutoff, not Lighthouse's TTI window. No coverage/tracing overhead in these samples, symmetric in every lane. All cells are median (min–max); bytes/requests unitless, time metrics ms.

Server RSS: N/A. resume-bench serves prerendered files and does not measure a per-framework SSR process or RSS; static server memory would not be framework SSR memory. No runtime/compiler changes were made, so this is a workload comparison, not an A/B runtime optimization claim.

Reproduce (Node 26.5.1 on PATH, nice -n 10; no installs):

```sh
node apps/resume-bench/run.ts --suite real --build --repeats 5 --port 4521 --out .artifacts/real-pages/2026-10-28-jd2 --report docs/benchmarks/2026-10-28-real-pages-jsdiet.md
```
